projects.title: TRACE
projects.summary: From an unfamiliar log source to an investigation you can inspect.
projects.context: Python · Elasticsearch · MCP · Schema generation · UI/UX
body: TRACE brings log onboarding, agent-assisted investigation, and independent evidence checks into one team project.

My work covers unknown-schema generation, validation and reuse, shared source onboarding, and the UI/UX. The interface follows a recorded SSH case through six stages, with source records, query receipts, and claim checks available to inspect.
The demo uses synthetic evidence. It supports analyst review; a verified citation is not a guarantee that an agent’s conclusion is correct.

projects.detailCaption: Interface detail · Recorded synthetic SSH case

projects.title: The Hidden Colouring
projects.summary: How do you prove you know an answer without giving it away?
body: An interactive guide to zero-knowledge proofs, built around a graph-colouring puzzle. Seal a colouring, challenge one edge, then open just the two answers needed to check it.
The Python protocol backs the lesson with SHA-256 commitments, public-transcript verification and tamper checks. The Protocol Lab lets visitors inspect messages and test altered openings.
This is an educational implementation with explicit assumptions, not production cryptography. Tests and empirical results do not prove zero knowledge.
projects.previewAlt: The Hidden Colouring lesson with a six-vertex colouring puzzle and an explanation of the prover and verifier.
projects.previewCaption: The actual lesson · Six chapters and a Protocol Lab
projects.detailAlt: Detail of the actual Hidden Colouring puzzle, showing six vertices connected by edges and three colours.
projects.detailCaption: Puzzle detail · From the interactive lesson

projects.title: Skopos
projects.summary: An Android module for choosing which contacts each app gets to see.
projects.detail: Policies support all contacts, selected contacts, or an empty dataset. Unconfigured apps retain native behaviour. Policies are stored through the Vector daemon; the manager stores only local UI preferences.

notes.label: Scope
notes.text: Per-app contact visibility, with selected contacts kept durable across edits.

notes.label: Privacy
notes.text: No runtime network dependency or telemetry, as documented in the repository.

notes.label: Requirements
notes.text: Android 16 / API 36 and a rooted Vector/libxposed environment.

body: All contacts, a few selected contacts, or none. Skopos applies those choices through Vector/libxposed; apps you haven’t configured keep their normal behaviour.
Built for Android 16 and a rooted Vector/libxposed setup. No runtime network dependency or telemetry.

about.heading: About
about.intro: I like working close to the system.
paragraphs: A lot of my learning starts with something I use: a phone, a Linux machine, or a service in my homelab. Maintaining those systems gives me practical questions to bring back to my security studies.

I’m interested in both the hands-on work and the decisions around it: how systems are operated, how risks are assessed, and what changes when AI becomes part of the system. That’s where my interests in cybersecurity, GRC, and AI security meet.

resumeProfile: Focused on cybersecurity, with practical experience building threat-hunting log workflows and cryptographic demonstrations. Combines Python implementation and integration testing with language-model research, Linux troubleshooting and clear technical communication to investigate security problems.
